title: First measured ON>OFF win for Darwin: temporal as-of retrieval beats flat-KB
summary: The Darwin gap-closer wave (6 tasks: retrieval benchmark, auto-extract, temporal reasoning, worktree isolation, onboarding loop, onboard-dropin) all built and held for merge. Strategically: the temporal task produced the FIRST measured benefit of the memory graph vs a baseline — as-of retrieval recall@5=1.0/MRR=1.0 vs latest-only flat-KB 0.6/0.6. This is the first concrete data point against the long-standing open risk ('ON-vs-OFF benefit unproven' from the v5 NO-WIN era). Caveat: it's one narrow benchmark (a fact that changed over time) where as-of is inherently advantaged; not yet a general competence win. But it's the proof-of-concept the 'Darwin = verifiable self-improvement' positioning needed. Pairs with the new retrieval-quality scorecard (recall@5=0.911 baseline) as the regression harness to measure all future memory work against.
